why: Kannapolis and Concord draw water from the Catawba River basin under an Inter-Basin Transfer agreement, so they follow the Catawba-Wateree Drought Management Advisory Group's Low Inflow Protocol, the river basin's shared drought plan, along with Harrisburg and Landis.
voluntary_tips: Water lawns and plants in the early morning or evening.
Fix dripping faucets, running toilets and plumbing leaks.
Take shorter showers; in a bath, use 1–2 inches less water.
Turn off the tap while brushing teeth, washing your face or shaving.
Run only full loads in the washer and dishwasher.
Don't let the faucet run while rinsing dishes or vegetables.
Use commercial car washes that recycle water; limit washing at home.
Check that irrigation systems use the right amount of water.

past_rules.label: Level 2 mandatory rules (in effect May 15 – Nov 2, 2026)
rules: Lawn, garden and plant watering only Tuesdays 8 p.m.–Wednesdays 8 a.m. and Saturdays 8 p.m.–Sundays 8 a.m.
Filling a new or drained pool needed a permit; topping off was allowed.
No residential car washing, and no home or driveway pressure washing.
No outdoor fountains unless supporting fish.
No washing public buildings, sidewalks or streets unless needed for health or safety.
Soaker hoses, drip irrigation and handheld watering were allowed for gardens.
Private wells not on City water were exempt.
